The Lagos State Government has set a target of securing at least 250 verified job opportunities for more than 2,500 job seekers participating in its 2026 employment fair, as it seeks to address the disconnect between the skills of young people and the demands of employers. The fair, organised by the Ministry of Wealth Creation and Employment, brought together job seekers, employers and recruitment professionals at the University of Lagos on Tuesday, with activities including direct recruitment, CV clinics and career counselling. The initiative formed part of the activities marking the fourth Lagos Employment Summit, which focused on bridging the gap between young people and employment opportunities. Governor Babajide Sanwo-Olu, represented by the Chairman of the Lagos State Civil Service Commission, Dapo Thomas, said the ability of an economy to provide sustainable livelihoods should be a major measure of its performance. He described youth empowerment as a priority of his administration, arguing that economic growth would remain incomplete if young people were unable to access opportunities to put their skills and talents to productive use. He explained that the job fair was designed to move beyond discussions about unemployment by providing a platform for direct engagement between prospective employees and organisations seeking qualified workers. “This initiative goes beyond discussions about unemployment; it provides practical opportunities for recruitment, career counselling, CV clinics, and direct engagement with prospective employers,” he said. The governor also highlighted the changing nature of employment, particularly the growing influence of artificial intelligence and emerging industries, saying his administration was committed to preparing young Lagosians for evolving labour market demands. In his keynote address, the Commissioner for Wealth Creation and Employment, Akinyemi Ajigbotafe, said the state government had continued to develop interventions aimed at improving employability, promoting entrepreneurship and connecting residents with decent employment opportunities. He described the job fair as an important component of the employment summit, providing a direct link between job seekers, employers and recruitment professionals. “This gathering represents another significant step in our collective commitment to expanding employment opportunities, strengthening workforce capacity and creating sustainable pathways to economic prosperity for the people of Lagos State,” Ajigbotafe said. The commissioner, however, acknowledged that unemployment was not simply a question of the availability of jobs, pointing to the mismatch between the competencies possessed by job seekers and the skills required by employers. His remarks highlighted the challenge facing employment initiatives that seek to connect graduates and other job seekers with available vacancies without adequately addressing the skills gap. The Executive Secretary of the Lagos State Employment Trust Fund, Feyisara Alayande, commended Sanwo-Olu for his commitment to employment generation, human capital development, entrepreneurship and inclusive economic growth. She called on employers, educational institutions, private sector organisations and development partners to strengthen collaboration in developing industry-driven training programmes. Alayande said educational and skills development systems must respond to changing labour market requirements to improve the prospects of young people seeking employment. Ayoola Babalola
